THE AWAKENING AND
THE VOID (1890s-1901)
• The Spontaneous Movement: Mass strikes
erupting in Tiflis and St. Petersburg.
• The Problem: Unorganized, politically
unconscious, fighting isolated battles
against individual masters.
• The Socialists: Operating in isolated,
abstract propaganda circles.
• The Disconnect: A heroic but futile
struggle shattering against the solid
wall of the tsarist autocracy.

THE ANATOMY OF NATIONALIST DEMANDS
THE NOBILITY (FEUDAL-MONARCHIST NATIONALISM)
• Demand: Liberation of Georgia.
• True Motive: Restore the Georgian kings and reclaim lost feudal privileges
from Russian rulers.
THE BOURGEOISIE (NATIONAL -DEMOCRATS)
• Demand: An Independent Georgia.
• True Motive: Build tariff walls to drive out foreign competitors and
artificially raise prices to control the local market.
THE PROLETARIAT (SOCIAL-DEMOCRATISM)
• Demand: Demolition of National Barriers.
• True Motive: Unite all workers across national lines to achieve the strength
necessary to overthrow the autocracy and capitalism.

see fit (though the Party advocates for unity),
LAVER 3: REGIONAL SELF-GOVERNMENT

THE BATTLE FOR DISCIPLINE: SCHISM
AT THE SECOND CONGRGRESS (1903)
The Expectation: The Congress was meant to
merge scattered forces into a single, indivisible
party under the banner of the old Iskra.
The Majority (Lenin): The trend of proletarian
firmness. Demands strict discipline,
centralized action, and a unified plan.
The Reality: The Congress splits over the
definition of party discipline and editorial
board seats.

THE ARCHITECTURE OF A REVOLUTION
PILLAR 1: IDEOLOGY
(VS. ECONOMISTS)
Imbuing the spontaneous movement
with scientific socialism.
PILLAR 3: DISCIPLINE
(VS. MENSHEVIKS)
Structuring the party as an exclusive
fortress of active, disciplined organizers,
not a banquet of sympathizers.
PILLAR 2: CENTRALISM
(VS. FEDERALISTS)
Demolishing national barriers to forge
a single, indivisible fighting force.
PILLAR 4: ACTION
(VS. AUTOCRACY)
Moving from political agitation to the
technical, organized guidance of an
armed uprising.
Synthesis Statement: A revolution cannot be spontaneous. It must be engineered,
organized, and led by a vanguard armed with theory and steeled in discipline.
